quick_notes.title: Polity Facts Recap
quick_notes.detail: Drafting (Ambedkar). USA (FR). 42nd (Mini Constitution). 17 (Untouchability). 32 (Heart/Soul). 35: Age for Pres. 110: Money. 368: Amend.
quick_notes.explanation: The Indian Constitution was drafted by a committee led by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, and the idea of Fundamental Rights (FR), which are basic rights guaranteed to every citizen, was borrowed from the United States of America (USA). The 42nd Amendment, passed in 1976, is called the Mini Constitution because it made many major changes, including adding the words Socialist and Secular to the Preamble. Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability, which is the practice of treating people as inferior based on their caste, and makes it a punishable offense. Article 32 gives citizens the right to directly approach the Supreme Court if their Fundamental Rights are violated, and it is called the Heart and Soul of the Constitution. Article 58 sets the minimum age for a person to become the President of India at 35 years. Article 110 defines a Money Bill, which is a type of law that deals only with taxes, government spending, or borrowing money. Article 368 lays down the procedure for amending, or changing, the Constitution itself.

quick_notes.title: Parliament Recap
quick_notes.detail: LS (550). RS (250/Perm). 108 (Joint). Zero Hour (12 PM). Mavalankar (1st Speaker).
quick_notes.explanation: The Parliament of India has two houses: the Lok Sabha, or House of the People, which can have a maximum of 550 elected members, and the Rajya Sabha, or Council of States, which can have a maximum of 250 members, of which 12 are nominated by the President for their expertise in fields like art or science, and the rest are elected by state assemblies. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house, meaning it is never fully dissolved, while the Lok Sabha is elected for a five-year term. A joint session of both houses is called under Article 108 of the Constitution to resolve a deadlock when one house rejects or does not agree with a bill passed by the other house. Zero Hour is an informal time at 12 PM (noon) in both houses when members can raise urgent matters without prior notice, though it is not mentioned in the official rules of procedure. The first Speaker of the Lok Sabha was Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar, who served from 1952 to 1956 and helped establish the office's traditions.

quick_notes.title: Amendment Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The 61st Amendment to the Constitution lowered the voting age for elections to the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies from 21 years to 18 years. The 73rd Amendment created a formal system of local self-government in rural areas, known as Panchayats, which are village councils elected by the people. The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, often called the Anti-Defection Law, says that an elected member of Parliament or a state legislature will lose their seat if they voluntarily give up their party membership or vote against their party's instructions without permission.

quick_notes.title: Books Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The Arthashastra is a book on statecraft and economics written by Kautilya, also known as Chanakya, who was a teacher and advisor to the first Mauryan emperor. The Indica is a lost account of India written by Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador who visited the court of Chandragupta Maurya. Gitanjali is a collection of poems by Rabindranath Tagore, for which he won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913. The Discovery of India is a book written by Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, while he was in prison, and it explores Indian history, culture, and philosophy.

quick_notes.title: Awards Recap
quick_notes.detail: Bharat Ratna (1954). Nobel (Tagore 1913). Oscar (Bhanu Athaiya). Phalke (Cinema).
quick_notes.explanation: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, established in 1954, given for exceptional service in any field. The Nobel Prize is an international award first given in 1901; Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, making him the first non-European to receive it. The Oscar is the Academy Award for excellence in filmmaking; Bhanu Athaiya was the first Indian to win an Oscar, for Best Costume Design for the film Gandhi in 1983. The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in cinema, named after the father of Indian cinema, Dhundiraj Govind Phalke, and is given for lifetime contribution to Indian cinema.

In SSC, this block provides around 4-6 questions. Today, we drill the numbers and names. If you see '324', you say 'Election'. If you see 'Bhanu Athaiya', you say 'Oscar'. Let's lock in the final GK marks today.
